revision.message:
Generate Anki CLI reference pages by root subcommand

Build a short CLI reference index and one child page for each root command,
including its complete nested help. Derive the hierarchy from the Cobra
command tree, package it as a generated directory, and keep generated
Markdown out of Git. Preserve aliases, inherited flags, RPC schemas, and
native help guidance.

OpenSpec-Change: projects/anki_as_code/openspec/changes/generate-cli-reference

Add a collection backend for prepared Anki servers

Add BackendCollection and its options object to the reusable Go backend.
It implements Backend while borrowing an already-started server: Start
opens the collection, Connection lends gated generated-client access, and
Stop closes the collection without stopping the borrowed backend. Keep the
public methods limited to Backend; restore destinations belong in options.

Open .anki2 databases directly. Restore .colpkg inputs through Anki into
an owned temporary directory by default, or an empty persistent destination
selected with RestoreDirectory. Observe consuming package exports and retain
files when cancelled native work makes cleanup uncertain. Callers stop the
collection before the process and clean retained temporary files after reaping.

Serialize startup with shutdown and reject preparation after a completed Stop.
Leave failed-start cleanup to explicit Stop instead of a hidden shutdown timeout.
Keep the connection adapter limited to Anki unary calls, tracking completed
export failures as consumed collections so their temporary files can be removed.
Track every unary caller and retain sticky uncertainty after unconfirmed
responses. Stop drains active callers within its context while ordinary
operations remain concurrent. Native E2E covers active and cancelled media
requests, concurrent progress access and cleanup after backend reaping.
Native E2E verifies overlapping lifecycle calls, storage/media persistence,
restore ownership, backend reuse, readiness, consuming exports and failures.
The anki_as_code integration is maintained separately in PRs #128 and #156;
its native, CLI and configuration E2E are verified against this library.

Extract shared Anki resource clients and snapshots

Centralize native resource access in internal/resource.Store. Construct Anki's
generated clients once on a caller-owned prepared connection, and read fresh
upstream deck, note-type, note and card messages plus existing preset names.
Preserve unmanaged resources and filtered-card references; return no partial
snapshot after errors and retain caller ownership of lifetime and returned data.

Include the selected deck ID when preset reads fail while preserving the native
error cause. Expose the generated clients for resource operations without forwarding every
method or creating generic CRUD models. Keep state bindings, config projection,
planning, mutation order, files and backend lifecycle outside this package.

Document the API and verify native operations, ordering, fresh reads, detached
values, cancellation and borrowed lifetime with JSON/native package artifacts.
Consumer integration belongs to PR #128 and PR #160; both stay master-based.

Integrate state commands with the native collection workflow

State commands now accept existing .anki2 databases and .colpkg archives through --collection. Compose the managed process and collection backends per operation, preserving direct database writes and using Anki native export for changed archives. App.WithCollection owns the scoped operation and cleanup; callers construct namespaced state stores directly from its prepared connection. Close the collection before the worker with bounded cleanup.

Extract the lifecycle and state CLI integration from #128 as an independent master-based prerequisite. Collection export, plan, apply and build remain placeholders; backend, state, config, codec and resource implementations are unchanged. #128 retains the overlap until this prerequisite merges.

Verify database and package state operations, batched imports, namespace isolation, no-op archives, cancellation, cleanup and preservation of native notes, reviewed cards, history, presets and media with the existing E2E coverage. Include the state flow diagram and current lifecycle documentation.

Add scoped managers for Anki backend lifetimes

Callers borrow prepared native backends through Manager.WithBackend or
ManagerCollection.WithCollection while managers own startup and ordered
cleanup. Share their lifecycle sequence through private withBackend, with
cancellation-independent cleanup and each manager's existing shutdown timeout.
Keep constructors, backend names and the public manager API unchanged.
Preserve callback errors and custom cancellation causes, and reap workers on
scope exit.

Keep source reservations, idle-worker caching, archive publication policy and
Anki-as-code services outside this independent library change. Native E2E
verifies readiness, process reaping, failure/cancellation/panic cleanup,
combined errors, delegated cleanup order, persistence and package restoration.
Validate repository quality, semantic lint, native consumers and documentation.

Integrate collection export with an isolated CLI

Expose collection export through the native workflow and existing exporter/config store while preserving source resources, state and archive bytes. Add config export for JSON-default or TOML config sets supplied through files or stdin. Keep plan, apply and build as placeholders; reconciliation remains in #128.

Keep concrete App in pkg/ankiascode and Cobra commands in internal/cli behind a private flat application interface. cmd/anki_as_code composes App and cli.New and handles signals. Group native commands under col with alias collection and text-only commands under config with alias conf; pass paths, namespace keys, protobuf objects and contexts explicitly.

Reuse the merged collection.Store for source reservations and archive publication. Its callbacks receive prepared grpc.ClientConnInterface; application workflows construct resource/state stores and exporters locally. Backend managers own native lifetime. Keep this PR against master; the collection-store and empty-media prerequisites are merged.

Verify isolated dispatch, flags, syntax, codecs, stream/error handling and native database/package export and state workflows. Emit native collections and TOML/JSON artifacts; validate repository quality, semantic lint, CLI builds and integrated documentation.

Remove backend managers from the native collection workflow

The collection store is the sole production manager consumer and already chooses a fresh stdin/stdout worker per source scope. Remove Manager, ManagerSTD, ManagerCollection and their constructors. Keep BackendSTD and BackendCollection with their explicit Start, Connection and Stop contracts.

Have collection.Store construct both owners directly, lend the prepared connection and close the collection before reaping the worker. Keep bounded cleanup in one private application helper, preserve callback/cancellation/crash errors and panic unwinding, and retain source reservations through cleanup. Existing archive publication and native restore-retention behavior remain unchanged.

Replace manager spies with real worker subprocess observations in the existing native store E2E. Verify process reaping, retained connection rejection, failed-start recovery, source reuse and callback success/error/cancellation/panic/crash paths. Retain direct backend, collection and application E2E, emit native collection artifacts, and validate quality, semantic lint, CLI and documentation builds without new dependencies.

The paired library API change is recorded in projects/anki_grpc/openspec/changes/remove-backend-managers.

Extract pure executable Anki collection planning

Separate planning from native execution so callers can prepare an executable CollectionPlan from supplied configs, a native snapshot and stored state without I/O or input mutation. internal/plan exposes one pure Build function; native execution and App integration remain in #128, independently targeting master.

Index captured Anki protobufs directly and resolve desired configs once into existing prepared protobufs. Share path/ID indexes across ownership checks and comparison. Produce typed operations and report entries together, with expected_state, proposed_bindings and path references for new objects instead of fabricated native IDs. Keep implementation indexes and resource moves private to planning.

Retain stable native member identities or original stored names, explicit move provenance and collision-free name releases. Protect untracked resources, template deck targets and resident filtered cards, including the cloze template-zero mapping. Permit tracked deck and note-type replacement without claiming untracked names. Anki owns native validation, normalization and generated-card migrations.

Native E2E captures exported TOML and snapshots before stopping its backend, then verifies deterministic detached plans, unchanged inputs/database, independent returned payloads, member drift, moves, empty namespace convergence and ownership protection. Extend the ownership fixture before refactoring; all seven baseline public reports remain unchanged. Emit executable JSON and native collection artifacts, document orchestration with Mermaid, and validate quality, semantic lint, consumers and integrated documentation.

Use folded-name order to prepare parents before mixed-case descendants. Keep preset aliases in the owned protobuf state and move disjoint bindings directly using existing resource maps, without duplicated ID, occupancy or replacement maps. Cover directory moves, occupied destinations, preset payload ownership and native deck replacement.

Keep desired decks in a single path index and sort emitted operations directly. Derive filtered-deck exclusions only for card assignments, reuse Resources for moved bindings and the pinned typed protobuf clone API, and use bounded member-ordinal slices. Verify declaration-order independence and resulting filtered kinds before implementation; preserve reports, ownership and executable-plan contracts.

regular collection package into private staging beside the destination,
rejects source aliases, and publishes only after successful native work.

both context cancellation and its custom cause for errors.Is.

packages, failed publication, cancellation, panic cleanup and invalid paths.
It emits collection archives and JSON state. No dependencies are added.

This is the independent build prerequisite for #128; application and CLI
integration remain there.

Link the Anki server into the CLI executable

Collection commands launch the current executable with server serve, so an installed
anki_as_code needs no companion executable, extraction or PATH discovery.
Keep process isolation and the existing bounded backend shutdown behavior.

Share the Rust transport, command dispatch and descriptor generator between the
standalone command and one argc/argv C ABI entry point linked through cgo using
existing Bazel rules. Require explicit worker configuration for Go application
collection operations, remove production discovery and the implicit standalone
worker runtime input, and configure the product worker with its own executable.
Name the Go host package ankiserver and its client-side lifecycle package
ankiclient. Keep server run as a generic native CLI passthrough and make
server serve delegate to server run serve. Rust owns serve dispatch, help,
transport arguments and validation.

Target master independently of API CLI PR #173. Verify installed native
operations with an empty PATH and unavailable temporary storage, missing worker
configuration, explicit library workflows, TCP/Unix interruption, and native
collection persistence. Test fixtures declare their executable inputs.

Generate service and method commands from all 25 compiled Anki schemas,
with protobuf JSON/TOML input and output and no per-method wrappers.

managed offline paths, borrowed connections and explicit TCP/Unix servers.

resources and make managed archive write-back explicit, enabled by the CLI
and existing application workflows independently of request outcomes.
Bound incomplete input by cancellation and timeout, and preserve linked
Unix server lifetime across client disconnections.

Verify installed execution, payloads, persistence, native connection
ownership and package boundaries through end-to-end workflows.
